Upcoming Federal Changes to MaineCare Eligibility for Some Non-citizens

Aug 20, 2026

We are writing to inform you about an upcoming change to MaineCare eligibility that may affect some of your MaineCare patients. This change is required by federal legislation signed into law in July 2025 (also called H.R.1, One Big Beautiful Bill, P.L.119-21, or Working Families Tax Cuts Act) that made changes to the Medicaid program nationally. These changes apply in all states, including Maine.

Beginning October 1, 2026, MaineCare eligibility is changing for some noncitizen groups. As a result, some individuals who currently receive full MaineCare benefits will no longer qualify for full coverage and will instead be eligible only for Emergency Services MaineCare. An explanation of covered benefits under Emergency Services MaineCare is available in the MaineCare Benefits Manual, Chapter 1, Section 1.02-4(D).

These changes will not affect children under age 21, or pregnant individuals through 12 months after the end of their pregnancy. Please note that the Office for Family Independence (OFI) is still completing the state rulemaking process to implement these federal requirements.

What You Should Know:

  • The eligibility changes are expected to take effect on October 1, 2026.
  • Members who are affected will receive a formal Notice of Decision from OFI before any eligibility changes take place. These notices are expected to be mailed in September 2026.
  • Some members received an early awareness letter in June or July 2026 to let them know they may be affected. This letter was informational only and is not an eligibility determination.

How You Can Help:

As a trusted healthcare provider, you can play an important role in helping your patients prepare for these changes by:

  • Encouraging patients to read any letters they receive from MaineCare or OFI.
  • Reminding patients to report any changes to their immigration status to OFI if it has changed since May 2026, as this could affect their eligibility.
  • Encouraging patients to continue using their MaineCare benefits to access covered healthcare services, including getting checkups and preventive care and refilling prescriptions, while they remain eligible.
  • Helping reassure patients that an early awareness letter does not mean their coverage has already changed.

Resources:

We developed resources to help providers understand these federal changes and answer patient questions. You can find these resources in this linked toolkit.

MaineCare and OFI will continue to share updates through provider e-messages and our webpage and other typical communication channels as additional information becomes available.

See the Non-citizen Resource Guide for resources that you can share with your patients to help support them in preparing for this change, and after their full MaineCare coverage ends. This list will be continually updated as we become aware of new resources.

If you have additional resources for us to add, please email MaineCare at Communications.MaineCare@maine.gov

If members have questions about covered services, please have them call Member Services at 1-800-977-6740.

Thank you for your continued partnership and for helping to ensure MaineCare members receive accurate information and access to the care they need.

item.title: US Labor Department finds Wisconsin food manufacturer repeatedly exposed workers to safety hazards following 2 incidents, 3 fatalities
item.description: JANESVILLE, WI – The U.S. Department of Labor has cited a Wisconsin-based food products manufacturer after two incidents involving industrial kettles releasing hot steam and liquid, causing three worker deaths and two serious injuries.Investigators with the department’s Occupational Safety and Health Administration responded to the first incident on Feb. 12, 2026, at IPMF LLC, operating as NaturPak. The incident involved the lid of an industrial kettle unexpectedly opening after a clogged vent line led to pressure building up, and then releasing steam, liquid, and organic material onto two employees nearby. One of the employees was also struck by an object and suffered a concussion. Both employees were hospitalized, and one later passed away because of complications from their injuries. A month later, OSHA investigators responded to another incident involving multiple worker hospitalizations on March 18, when a kettle lid opened while under pressure releasing steam, hot liquid, and organic material, burning three workers. Two workers were fatally injured and another hospitalized. OSHA issued the employer one serious citation for the design and usage of kettles leading to pressure and thermal burn hazards; a repeat citation for exposing workers to falls to lower levels; and an other-than-serious citation for failing to notify employees working adjacent to permit-required confined spaces.OSHA also issued serious citations for exposing workers to thermal hazards without quick access to emergency water. The employer also received citations for exposing workers to falls into the kettles and for failure to assess personal protective equipment for thermal risks. In addition, OSHA issued repeat citations for failure to develop, document, and utilize lockout/tagout procedures for the kettles and failure to train employees on lockout/tagout procedures. The agency issued citations with $115,850 in penalties related to the inspection opened on Feb. 12 and $248,250 in penalties

The Employment Situation in Maine - July 2026

August 21, 2026

Released: 10 a.m. Friday, August 21, 2026

Contact: Mark McInerney, (207) 620-0197

The Employment Situation in Maine - July 2026

The 3.1 unemployment rate was unchanged for the fourth consecutive month. Nonfarm wage and salary jobs have remained within a narrow range for 27 consecutive months.

Seasonally Adjusted Statewide Labor Force Estimates

The unemployment rate remained at 3.1 percent in July. Unemployment rates have remained within a narrow range between 3.1 and 3.3 percent for 23 consecutive months. Unemployment has been below four percent for 55 months, the longest duration on record. Maine's unemployment rate has been below the U.S. average for more than 18 years, and remains below the long-term average of 5.4 percent for the state since 1976. Unemployment averaged 4.2 percent for New England and 4.1 percent for the U.S. in the month.

The labor force participation rate averaged 59 percent in the last three months, modestly lower than the three months through April. The employment-to-population ratio was also modestly lower in the three months through July compared to the three months prior.

Seasonally Adjusted Statewide Nonfarm Jobs Estimates

Preliminary seasonally adjusted estimates indicate that in July, nonfarm wage and salary jobs were little changed from June. Most sectors exhibited little net job change over-the-month.

Job estimates have stayed within a narrow range near 660,000 for 27 consecutive months (estimates ranging less than one half of one percent higher or lower each month). Over the last year, a decrease in jobs in the professional and business services sector and smaller decreases in other sectors were mostly offset by increases that were also spread across several sectors.

These estimates are derived from two monthly surveys. The Current Population Survey collects information from households on labor force status, including labor force participation, employment, and unemployment. The Current Employment Statistics survey collects information from nonfarm employers by industry on the number of wage and salary jobs, hours worked, and wages paid to individuals on their payrolls. Both surveys are administered by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics. Preliminary estimates from the two surveys sometimes diverge in direction or magnitude of change. Over extended periods they tend to be more aligned. The Current Population Survey of households was not conducted during the federal government shutdown that began in October 2025, no labor force estimates are available for that month.

Not Seasonally Adjusted County and Metro Area Labor Force Estimates

On a not seasonally adjusted basis the statewide unemployment rate was 3.0 percent. Rates were at least 0.3 percentage points higher than that in eight counties, at least 0.3 points lower than that in four, and close to the average in four. Rates were lowest in coastal counties and highest along the northern rim of the state.

Among the three metro areas, unemployment was below the statewide average in Portland-S. Portland, and close to the average in Bangor and Lewiston-Auburn.

Labor force estimates for substate areas, including unemployment rates, are not seasonally adjusted. Because of this, estimates for a certain month should be compared to the same month in other years and should not be compared to other months in the same or other years.

Attention Trading Partners: MIHMS Upgrade October Payment Cycle Changes and System Access Limitations

Aug 21, 2026

As previously communicated, the Office of MaineCare Services (OMS) is preparing to launch an upgraded version of MIHMS, MaineCare’s claims processing system. The upgrade is currently scheduled to go live on October 10, 2026. To support a smooth transition, OMS must implement temporary system access limitations and adjustments to payment cycles in October.

From Friday, October 2 at 8:00 PM until Monday, October 12 at 8:00 AM, MIHMS will be in a “data freeze” while OMS completes final system readiness and transition activities.

Changes to October payment cycles:

Review this information and plan billing accordingly to prepare for the transition.

Payment Cycle Date Payment Impact Claim Submission Deadline for Inclusion in Payment Cycle*
Wednesday, 9/30/26 Last regular payment before the data freeze Friday, 9/25/26, 5:00 AM
Thursday, 10/1/26 Extra payment before the data freeze Wednesday, 9/30/26, 5:00 AM
There will be no payment on Wednesday, October 7.
Thursday, 10/15/26 First payment after data freeze, in upgraded system

Secure File Transfer Protocol (SFTP) submission: Continuous through data freeze up to Tuesday, 10/13/26, 2:00 PM

Portal submission:

Before data freeze: Friday, 10/2/26, 7:59 PM

After data freeze: Tuesday, 10/13/26, 2:00 PM
Wednesday, 10/21/26 Regular payment, in upgraded system Friday, 10/16/26, 5:00 AM

*As always, timely submission does not guarantee that the claim will process in time for the next payment cycle. OMS may take up to 30 days to process and pay a claim, depending on any edits or issues that may cause the claim to pend for manual review, as well as other processing requirements that may require the full 30-day timeframe.

Non-claims payments:

By September 1, OMS will communicate with any providers expecting non-claims payments that may be affected by the schedule described above.

Preparing for the changes to October payment cycles:

Beginning September 1, 2026 7:00 AM, OMS will return the HealthPAS Online Portal to its previous regular operating hours. Providers will again have 24/7 access to the portal, for additional flexibility and time to submit claims outside of standard business hours. 

We strongly encourage providers to submit claims approaching timely filing limits in the next few weeks to avoid potential submission delays. The planned data freeze does not modify existing Medicaid timely filing requirements. Providers remain responsible for ensuring claims are submitted within the established timely filing guidelines.

Other system access limitations:

Providers can find other expected impacts of the data freeze in this FAQ. Topics include:

  • HealthPAS Online Portal, including impacts on submitting claims, submitting prior authorizations, and checking member eligibility
  • Provider Enrollment Application (PEA)
  • Value-Based Purchasing Management System (VMS) Portal
  • Paper & fax document submissions
  • Provider Services & Member Services call centers
  • Value Added Network (VAN) Trading Partners
  • Prior authorizations for prescriptions and behavioral health services
  • Electronic Visit Verification (EVV)

You can also check the OMS Provider Resources webpage, in the first box of information called “Health PAS Online Portal,” for the most recent information about the upgrade.

For questions or clarifications, please contact Provider Services at 1-866-690-5585. Please note, Provider Services does not have additional information beyond what is shared in this message and in the FAQ linked above.

2027 MaineCare Eligibility Changes: Information, Resources, and Partner Briefing

Aug 21, 2026

The federal government is making changes to MaineCare (Maine’s Medicaid program). These changes apply to Medicaid programs across the country. Last week the Office of MaineCare Services (OMS) sent out a Save-the-Date for an August 24, 2026, partner and provider briefing on upcoming changes to MaineCare eligibility. There is still time to register!  

The Office for Family Independence (OFI) and OMS are working together to implement these changes as smoothly as possible to avoid disruptions in coverage for eligible Mainers. Our goal is to provide Mainers with clear, accurate, and actionable information so they can confidently understand how these changes may affect them. 

What is changing?  

As of January 1, 2027, the following MaineCare eligibility changes will start:   

For MaineCare Expansion adults:  

  • New Work Requirements; and  

  • Eligibility renewals every 6 months instead of every 12 months.  

For all MaineCare members:  

  • Reductions in retroactive coverage.   

MaineCare Expansion members are adults between 19 and 64 years old who have MaineCare based on their income. They do not meet the Social Security disability guidelines or have Medicare.

What can MaineCare Members Do Now? 

The most important things MaineCare members can do right now are: 

  • Keep their contact information up to date with OFI,  

  • Read any letters they receive, 

  • Continue renewing their coverage as required, and  

  • Continue using their MaineCare benefits. 

We know that members rely on their healthcare providers for trusted information about MaineCare. We appreciate the value that adds, as well as the additional work. Our goal is to support providers through these changes 

Resources to be aware of right now include:  

  • Save the Date: DHHS Partner Briefing on Federal Medicaid Work Requirements and Increased Renewals on August 24, 2026 – register today 

  • Webpages: Federal Changes webpage, MaineCare.gov/FederalChanges, and Work Requirements webpage, MaineCare.gov/Work 

  • Communication tools: A Partner Communications Toolkit for the MaineCare Expansion member changes is available on the Work Requirements webpage. 

  • We are working closely with Maine’s Medicaid Ombudsman program, operated by Consumers for Affordable Health Care, to support community partners who assist Mainers with navigating the MaineCare application and renewal process.  

  • OMS will share a message next week with information about an upcoming pathway for providers to share data with us to support MaineCare eligibility determinations.  

Please note: Maine is still working through key details with the federal government, and we will continue to communicate about who is affected and the steps Expansion members will need to take as we approach 2027.

Final Notification to Trading Partners about Taking Action Now Before MaineCare’s New Online Portal Goes Live

Aug 24, 2026

A refreshed and upgraded MIHMS is coming in mid October 2026. The Office of MaineCare Services (OMS), in partnership with Gainwell Technologies, is launching an upgraded MIHMS, to bring enhanced security, improved usability, and a more modern experience to better support your day-to-day work. 

The upgrade will include a new “MaineCare Partner Portal” that will replace what is known today as the “Health PAS Online Portal.” Please note that, until the October go-live, we will continue using the name “Health PAS Online Portal” in communications related to current functionality. 

You can read more about the benefits to providers and members on the Health PAS Online Portal. 

Trading Partners Preparation 

This is the final notice reminding trading partners to take action to prepare for the transition to the upgraded online portal, called the MaineCare Partner Portal. 

Trading partners include providers, billing agents, health plans, clearinghouses, and business associates. Trading partners have an important role to play in supporting a smooth transition and uninterrupted access to the portal after go-live. 

Portal Access Impacts and Required Actions Before Go‑Live 

The preparation activities and changes below will improve system security by ensuring the right people have the right access, at go-live and ongoing. Most actions are only for Admin (R7) users.  

Most important: Providers with duplicate emails need to make changes to their portal user accounts now to assist with account migration to the upgraded portal. On September 1, we will terminate current Admin (R7) user accounts that share an email address with another user account. We will not terminate Admin (R7) user accounts if they are the only Admin (R7) on the Trading Partner account. 

If a user account is terminated and they still need portal access, another user with Admin Rights (R7) can invite the terminated user using a unique email address, not the one previously used.  

Activity/Change 

Your Action 

Why it Matters 

What’s Next? 

At go-live, MaineCare will only migrate Admin (R7) accounts to the new portal. 

  

MaineCare will not migrate inactive accounts. 

Designate at least one active Admin (R7) per organization, and two for backup coverage. 

  

Trading Partners with large user populations should plan for sufficient Admin (R7) coverage to avoid access delays after go-live; we recommend one Admin (R7) per 25 users. 

  

Remove inactive Admin (R7) accounts. 

After go-live, Admin (R7) users will need to re-invite all other active users. More Admin (R7) users mean less re-invitation work for each user. 

  

Trading Partners have an existing and ongoing responsibility to remove inactive users to help keep our systems and data secure. 

  

We will monitor the number and activity of Admin (R7) users per Trading Partner and will reach out to individual Trading Partners if needed. 

In the new portal, your username will be your email address. 

MaineCare will not migrate accounts that share an email address. 

Confirm that each active Admin (R7) user account has its own unique email address. 

OMS will deactivate accounts that continue to share email addresses as we approach go-live. 

After go-live, Admin (R7) users will need immediate access to the portal to invite other users and avoid disruption in Trading Partner work. 

We will monitor accounts that share email addresses and will reach out to individual Trading Partners if needed. 

Admin (R7) users will invite other users to the portal and designate your roles after go-live. 

  

Admin (R7) will be able to choose from ~40 permissions, compared to 9 today. 

Prepare to invite users after go-live: 

  • Know who needs a user account in the new portal 

  • Know the permission level each user will need to have 

  

Admin (R7) users will need to invite other users shortly after go-live to avoid a disruption in Trading Partner work. 

  

We will share more information during trainings including role definitions, templates, and other guidance. 

 For questions, please email Provider Services or call 1-866-690-5585.

Attention Trading Partners: Training for New MaineCare Partner Portal

Aug 25, 2026

We have previously shared that a refreshed and upgraded MIHMS, with a new “MaineCare Partner Portal,” is coming in October 2026. This will replace the current HealthPAS Online Portal. We are now inviting trading partners to register for training starting September 8, 2026 to help you prepare for the transition to the new portal. Trading partners include providers, billing agents, health plans, clearinghouses, and business associates. Trading partners have an important role to play in supporting a smooth transition and uninterrupted access to the portal after go-live.

Gainwell Technologies will be leading live virtual instructor-led training sessions. These courses will provide the knowledge and skills needed to navigate the new portal, complete daily business functions, and use new portal features. Training demonstrations, materials, and supporting resources will help participants prepare for a successful transition.

Steps you need to take to attend training

  • Review the available training topics listed below and identify the sessions that align with your role and responsibilities.
  • Use the LMS registration (instructions below) to create an account, access the training catalog, and enroll in applicable sessions.
  • Contact Gainwell (instructions below) if you need assistance.
  • Recorded sessions and other training materials will be available in the LMS after training sessions for ongoing reference.

MaineCare Partner Portal Training Sessions

Course Name

Description

ME - TPT - Migrated Trading Partner Log In and Account Maintenance Training (ILC)

Learn how to complete first-time login activities, configure multi-factor authentication (MFA), manage user accounts and permissions, perform account maintenance activities, and understand electronic data interchange (EDI) certification requirements and status monitoring. This course is only for Admin (R7) users.

ME - TPT - Trading Partner Registration and Account Maintenance Training (ILC)

Learn how to register a new Trading Partner account, complete account activation, manage users and permissions, associate providers and billing agents, navigate the portal, and maintain account information.

ME - TPT - Authorization, Referrals and Certifications Training (ILC)

Learn how to submit and manage authorizations, process referrals, monitor certification requests and statuses, and access related portal functionality.

ME - TPT - Dental Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC)

Learn how to submit dental claims, monitor claim processing and status, and navigate claim-related portal functions.

ME - TPT - Institutional Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC)

Learn how to submit institutional claims, monitor claim processing and status, and navigate claim-related portal functions.

ME - TPT - Professional Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC)

Learn how to submit professional claims, monitor claim status, review payment information, access remittance advice, and complete related claim activities.

ME - TPT - MaineCare Partner Public Portal Training (ILC)

Learn about publicly available portal functionality, portal resources and reference materials, secure messaging, Trading Partner tools, and available resources.

 

LMS Access and Course Registration Instructions

Use the following steps to register for MaineCare Partner Portal training. Multiple sessions are available for each course to allow for scheduling flexibility.

  1. Go to the LMS registration site: https://mmislearningcenter.myabsorb.com/#/login.
  2. Sign in using your existing account or click Sign Up on the right side of the window to create a new account.
  3. If you need a new account, enter the enrollment key: De8pO9CBYXYB-aOCY8qp on the Sign Up window.
  4. Complete the required registration information to create your account. Note: You can enter your workplace address.
  5. The Learner Dashboard appears. From this window, you can access previous trainings, search for and enroll in the appropriate training sessions, and review your transcript.
  6. To locate the appropriate courses, search using “TPT” or the course name from the table above in the search bar at the top of the window or by opening the Course Catalog tile.
  7. Click Choose Session for each course you need to complete, then enroll in the session that best fits your schedule.
  8. You will receive an email confirmation regarding the success of your enrollment. Additionally, you will receive a Microsoft Teams calendar event for each session.
  9. On the day of the training, access the training via one of the following methods:
    • Access the Teams Meeting hyperlink from the course confirmation email.
    • Click the Microsoft Teams meeting hyperlink within the Outlook/Teams calendar event.
    • Access My Courses in the LMS and click the appropriate Microsoft Teams meeting hyperlink.

Do not forward meeting invitations to other attendees. Each participant must register through the LMS to receive course acces

item.title: MHRC Guidance on HUD Change to Definition of Assistance Animal
item.description: Maine Human Rights Commission # 51 State House Station, Augusta, ME 04333-0051 Physical location: 19 Union Street, Augusta, ME 04330 ■ ■Phone (207) 624-6290 Fax (207) 624-8729 TTY: Maine Relay 711 www.maine.gov/mhrc Kit Thomson Crossman Barbara Archer Hirsch EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR COMMISSION COUNSEL MAINE HUMAN RIGHTS COMMISSION Public Guidance Statement RE: HUD's New Emotional Support Animal Enforcement Guidance and Maine Housing Providers' Continuing Obligations Under the Maine Human Rights Act August 4, 2026 What Has Changed at the Federal Level On May 22, 2026, the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) issued an enforcement memorandum announcing that it will no longer find reasonable cause in housing complaints involving emotional support animals (ESAs). In other words, animals that provide comfort, companionship, or otherwise mitigate the effects of a person’s disability but have not been individually trained to perform specific disability-related tasks are no longer protected at the federal level. Going forward, HUD will pursue enforcement only where an animal has been trained to perform work or tasks directly related to a person's disability (essentially, HUD has imported the Americans with Disabilities Act's narrower "service animal" definition into Fair Housing Act enforcement). HUD simultaneously rescinded its 2020 guidance, which had for years provided meaningful protections to individuals who rely on ESAs as part of their disability-related care. After 35 years without updating its regulations in this area, the federal government's chosen solution has been, perhaps unsurprisingly, to reduce protections rather than clarify them. The Maine Human Rights Commission takes note of this development. We also take note that it changes nothing in Maine. Maine DEP Initiates Legal Action Against Mallinckrodt US LLC to Address Cleanup Failures at Orrington Site

Maine Department of Environmental Protection sent this bulletin at 08/25/2026 03:45 PM EDT

--- PRESS RELEASE ---

For Immediate Release

 

Maine DEP Initiates Legal Action Against Mallinckrodt US LLC to Address Cleanup Failures at Orrington Site

 

AUGUSTA, August 25, 2026 — The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) filed a formal complaint today in Penobscot County Superior Court against Mallinckrodt US LLC (Mallinckrodt). The complaint details the failure by Mallinckrodt to complete cleanup of the former Holtrachem site located along the Penobscot River in Orrington, Maine, one of Maine’s most contaminated sites. Mallinckrodt has not met the remediation standards required in the DEP’s 2008 Designation of Uncontrolled Hazardous Substance Site and Order, that was affirmed in 2010 by the Board of Environmental Protection (BEP) in its own slightly modified order, affirmed in 2012 by the Maine Business and Consumer Docket, and finally affirmed in 2014 by the Maine Supreme Judicial Court sitting as the Law Court.

The former Holtrachem site was a chloralkali manufacturing facility, which made chemicals commonly used in the pulp and paper industry. Historic operations resulted in a significant amount of contamination, including highly toxic mercury and chloropicrin, in surrounding soils, groundwaters, and the Penobscot River. Site-specific standards were established by the DEP and BEP Orders to ensure that the site would be cleaned up in a manner that would protect public health, safety, and the environment.  Despite these Orders, large areas of soils still remain on site that exceed the site-specific cleanup standards.

The DEP has worked diligently to provide oversight during cleanup of the former Holtrachem site to ensure that Mallinckrodt conducts remediation in compliance with the DEP and BEP Orders. While progress has been made, it began to slow down as early as 2018 when Mallinckrodt began the first of several attempts to seek relief from meeting the Orders’ requirements. Since 2023, Mallinckrodt has ceased any meaningful progress toward remediation at the site.

Prior to today’s filing, two Notices of Violation (NOVs) were issued to Mallinckrodt on March 19, 2025, and October 22, 2025. These NOVs provide more detailed information about Mallinckrodt’s failure to comply with the DEP and BEP Orders. Copies of these NOVs are available on the DEP Mallinckrodt webpage.

The Department is seeking injunctive relief from the Penobscot Superior Court and civil penalties for ongoing violations.

Specifically, if plan materials merely mention that a health-contingent wellness program is available, without describing its terms, the plan or issuer is not required to disclose the availability of a reasonable alternative standard to qualify for the reward under the wellness program.“The experimental nature of wellness programs enables them to drive significant and clinically meaningful health maintenance and improvements,” said Assistant Secretary for Employee Benefits Security Daniel Aronowitz. “This guidance makes clear to sponsors and issuers that, as long as they are offering reasonably designed, and otherwise non-discriminatory wellness programs, they will not be penalized for wanting to help motivate the people they cover to make efforts to improve their health.”Employers and workers can contact EBSA at askebsa.dol.gov or call 866-444-3272 toll-free for help with private sector job-based retirement and health plans.Read the FAQs on wellness programs in employer-sponsored health plans.

item.description: WATSONTOWN, PA – The U.S. Department of Labor has cited a brick manufacturer with three willful and four serious violations for knowingly exposing its workers to unsafe levels of respirable silica dust at its Watsontown plant.On Feb. 12, 2026, investigators with the department’s Occupational Safety and Health Administration inspected General Shale Brick Inc. – doing business as Watsontown Brick Company – as part of the agency’s Site‑Specific Targeting inspection plan and national emphasis program on silica as well as a review of the company’s injury and illness records. OSHA found that workers in Plant 3, where molded brick is made, breathed in silica dust above safe limits. The company knew about the exposure but failed to fix the problem or require workers to wear respirators.OSHA also determined the company failed to test workers’ respirator fit each year, did not establish regulated areas where employees are exposed to silica, did not check silica exposure levels for all silica-involved jobs, and did not provide required medical exams for workers exposed to silica for more than 30 days a year. A past violation for missing respirator fit tests, at the company’s Augusta, Georgia site, led to an added repeat violation.OSHA issued three willful, four serious, one repeat, and one other-than-serious violation, with proposed penalties of $496,528.The company has 15 business days from receipt of its citations to comply, request an informal conference with OSHA’s area director, or contest the findings before the independent Occupational Safety and Health Review Commission. Check the OSHA establishment search page periodically for any changes in the inspection or penalty status.Learn more about protecting workers from silica hazards. Employers can also contact the agency for free help meeting OSHA safety standards.
